approval.trigger: No review conditions user connections: any user you send to the authorize URL can grant a token immediately, with no stated user cap. Review exists only for the public Power-Up directory listing: register the Power-Up, sign the Joint Developer's Agreement, complete all admin fields (Support Email and Privacy Policy are required), and submit; the review team installs your Power-Up on their own board and checks it against the Power-Up Guidelines.
approval.wait: Directory review 'usually takes two or more weeks' depending on feedback rounds (stated). Launch-marketing approvals typically take 5-10 business days (stated)

blockers.detail: On the Trello Auth tab you must add the origins Trello may redirect to after consent (wildcards like https://*.myapplication.com and http://localhost allowed). The docs warn verbatim: 'If your API key has no allowed origins set, then no redirect URL will work.' Nothing fails at key-generation time; it fails silently at your first real user.
blockers.howToClear: Set Allowed Origins as part of initial setup, including your production and staging origins.
blockers.title: Empty Allowed Origins blocks every redirect

blockers.detail: User tokens 'grant access to the entire user's account' and remain able to reach boards and Workspaces the user gains access to in the future. Tokens should always be securely stored; the API key, by contrast, may be public. There is no narrower containment to design around beyond the three scopes.
blockers.howToClear: Vault tokens like credentials, request expiration=never only when you truly need it, and handle revocation gracefully.
blockers.title: Tokens are account-wide and powerful

blockers.detail: The authorize route has no refresh mechanism: token lifetime is whatever expiration you chose at request time (1hour, 1day, 30days, never). An expired token returns 401 invalid token and 'the Power-Up or integration should ask the user to re-authorize'.
blockers.howToClear: Choose expiration deliberately per product need (never for persistent agents), and build the re-authorization path as a first-class flow.
blockers.title: No refresh tokens; expiry means re-authorize

flavor.recommended: A registered Power-Up (to obtain the API key and secret) plus the 1/authorize token flow for user connections
flavor.why: There is no OAuth 2.0 and no client-credentials app model. The docs offer exactly two ways to get a per-user token: Trello's proprietary 1/authorize consent route (the mainstream path) or legacy OAuth 1.0a. A standalone SaaS does not need an in-Trello Power-Up UI or a directory listing for users to authorize.

humanMust: Register the Power-Up and generate the API key (Trello account + a Workspace you administer)
Sign the Joint Developer's Agreement if you pursue a directory listing
Users click Allow on Trello's consent page
name: Trello
nuances: Only three scopes exist: read, write, account. The account scope is required to read the member's email, and only the granting user's email.

Token delivery is fragile by modern standards: with response_type=token and no return_url, the token is displayed on a page for the user to hand back; with fragment it lands in the URL hash for your JavaScript to capture. There is no server-to-server code exchange outside OAuth 1.0a.
Users manage your access at trello.com/u/{username}/account and can revoke anytime; tokens can also be deleted via the API's /1/tokens DELETE.
Power-Up assets must be served over HTTPS and CORS-configured for trello.com, since Trello loads the connector in an iframe.
Documented quirk: the REST API client's getToken()/isAuthorized() may misbehave on current Chrome due to third-party storage partitioning.
prerequisites: A Trello account and a Workspace you administer
An HTTPS-hosted iframe connector page (the Power-Up's hidden iframe)

steps.detail: At trello.com/apps/admin, pick the Workspace you administer, click New, and fill the form (name, iframe connector URL: the HTTPS page Trello loads as the Power-Up's hidden iframe, plus other fields).
steps.title: Register a Power-Up

steps.detail: Open the Power-Up > Trello Auth tab > Generate a new API Key. Copy the API key (the docs stress: the key, not the secret). Note the application secret on the same tab if you will use OAuth 1.0a signing.
steps.title: Generate the API key

steps.detail: Same tab: add the origins Trello may redirect to after consent (wildcards allowed; localhost allowed for development). With no origins set, no redirect URL will work.
steps.title: Configure Allowed Origins

steps.detail: Send each user to trello.com/1/authorize with key, name, scope (comma-separated read, write, account), expiration (1hour, 1day, 30days, never), response_type=token, and return_url + callback_method=fragment (token returns in the URL hash) or postMessage for popups. Alternatively implement OAuth 1.0a with the three 1/OAuth* endpoints.
steps.title: Build the authorization flow

steps.detail: Call the API with key + token as query parameters, an Authorization: OAuth header, or in request bodies. On denial the fragment returns token=<redacted> plus error=; revoked or expired tokens return 401 invalid token, your cue to ask the user to re-authorize.
steps.title: Call the API with key + token

steps.detail: (Only for a public listing) Complete all admin fields including Support Email and Privacy Policy, sign the Joint Developer's Agreement, and submit via the developer support form with your Connector URL and Power-Up ID. The review team tests on their own board and iterates by email; launch is at an agreed date.
steps.time: Submission ~30 min; review two or more weeks (stated)
steps.title: (Optional) Submit for the Power-Up directory

tagline: There is no OAuth 2.0 here at all: a Power-Up registration gives you an API key, and users hand you a token via Trello's own authorize page (or legacy OAuth 1.0a). Three scopes, token expiry you choose, review only for a directory listing.

time.active: ~15 min of registration and key setup + ~1 hr of flow code
time.total: Same day for user connections; two or more weeks only if you want the public directory listing
